problem: Prior MLLM visual-search work operates on a single static 2D image with crop/zoom tools, so it is non-interactive and disembodied. Embodied navigation platforms are limited to household scenes or low-realism simulators, leaving visually crowded in-the-wild scenes (stations, malls, streets) unstudied.
motivation: Humans search 360° by coordinating head and eye movements, and reasoning is intermittent, invoked only at critical decision points. Turning real 360° panoramas into a lightweight closed-loop simulator, where a head rotation renders a new perspective view, allows embodied active search in the wild without 3D simulators or robot hardware.
key_idea: Model humanoid head rotation as a tool call over a 360° panorama so an MLLM actively searches for objects or paths, and post-train it with SFT then multi-turn GRPO on the new H*Bench benchmark.
insight: SFT contributes most of the gain (HOS 14.83→40.83, HPS 6.44→23.00) while RL adds little (+6.55 / +1.94) and even hurts medium and extreme HPS, so post-training fixes grounding and exploration but not the physical and socio-spatial commonsense that path search needs. 2D search models near saturation on V* Bench (88.2% / 88.0%) collapse on H*Bench (2.5% / 11.6%), showing that passive-data skills do not transfer to embodied search. Object-search and path-search training transfer to each other (HPS 6.4→20.7 and HOS 14.8→29.5).
method: Task formulation: the environment is a single 360° panorama, observations are narrow-FoV perspective views o(φ,γ), and the goal is the direction (φ*,γ*) that maximizes task success. HOS needs yaw and pitch to foveate the target, while HPS needs only yaw aligned with a navigable path.

Agent policy: a tool-augmented MLLM outputs a chain of thought plus an action each turn, conditioned on the current view, instruction and history. The actions are rotate(Δyaw,Δpitch) and submit(yaw,pitch), which ends the episode.

H*Bench: about 3,000 annotated task instances from panoramic videos (up to 7680×3840), 12 countries, 6 scene categories and 18 scene types. Each has 4 start orientations, giving 12,000 episodes. Annotators draw a bounding box that is back-projected to give the GT direction, and difficulty levels are defined (HOS by initial visibility, HPS by textual cues and cue-path alignment).
Cold-start data: GPT-4o writes CoT rationales for human-optimal actions, which annotators then refine (250 hours, 6 annotators), yielding 2,000 multi-turn trajectories for SFT.
Stage 1 SFT: full-parameter SFT of Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct for 3 epochs with LLaMA-Factory on mixed HOS and HPS data (250 instances each), lr 1e-5.

Stage 2 multi-turn GRPO: built on VAGEN, 70 steps, batch 32, lr 1e-7, KL β=0.01, group size 8, 5 or 10 turn limit. The reward is a rule-based format (0.5) plus correctness (0.5), with optional distance-to-goal shaping for HPS.
Evaluation metric: success if the submitted direction falls in a bbox-centered tolerance region, with τφ=30°, τγ=20° for HOS and τφ=10° for HPS. Max 10 turns, unfinished episodes count as failures.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (SFT then GRPO, full fine-tuning); baselines are frozen proprietary and open MLLMs
setting.training_data: 500 SFT instances (250 HOS + 250 HPS; the text also cites 2,000 CoT multi-turn trajectories generated by GPT-4o and human-refined) plus the remaining ~1,500 annotated instances for RL, all from H*Bench panoramas
setting.observation: perspective (narrow-FoV) RGB views rendered from a 360° panorama, with green-cross camera center, at 1280×720 in training and 1920×1080 in evaluation; up to 5 images in context
setting.action_space: rotate(Δyaw,Δpitch) in degrees and submit(yaw,pitch) on the panorama sphere
setting.simulator: custom panorama-based lightweight simulator (real 360° panoramas), no 3D simulator

numbers_note: Results are on the paper's own H*Bench (no standard nav benchmark). The V* Bench numbers (HVS-3B 65.5%) and the H*Bench overall figure (38.4%) appear only in a figure and text, so they are not tabulated. No table caption states the split name, so 'test' is assumed.
results: HVS-3B raises Qwen2.5-VL-3B from 14.83 to 47.38 on object search and from 6.44 to 24.94 on path search. This beats Gemini2.5-Pro on HOS (31.96) but falls short of it on HPS (33.00). The best open-weight baseline is Gemma-3-4B (17.13 HOS, 14.44 HPS), and GPT-4o scores 19.75 / 23.69.
limitations: Path search remains hard (24.94 vs Gemini 33.00). RL degrades medium and extreme HPS, likely from reward hacking, and reward shaping only helps the easy split.

The panorama simulator has a single fixed viewpoint with only head rotation, so there is no locomotion or full 3D, and evaluation is a direction-tolerance check rather than actual navigation or manipulation.
Small SFT and RL dataset (~3,000 instances), 3B model only, and 10-turn cap with unfinished episodes counted as failures.
